==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Selenium&min=Selenium&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Plugins/SeleniumTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Selenium&min=Selenium&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using OpenQA.Selenium;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Chrome;
using VerifyTests.Selenium;

// Verify.Selenium: Verifies a Selenium WebDriver page or element as both its html and a screenshot png.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.HeadlessBrowsers
// Note: Each verification writes two files: the html and a png screenshot.
// Note: Screenshots vary between operating systems and renderers, so an image comparer, or
// VerifierSettings.UseSsimForPng(...), is what keeps CI stable.
// Note: --disable-lcd-text makes text rendering reproducible; existing screenshots have to be
// re-accepted once after adding it.
// Note: The Selenium.WebDriver.ChromeDriver package puts a chromedriver in the output directory,
// so nothing has to be on the PATH, but its version has to match the installed Chrome.
// Note: SocketWaiter is defined separately by each of the three headless browser packages, here in
// VerifyTests.Selenium.
// Note: WaitForIsReady() and GetSource() are internal to the package. The converter calls them
// before capturing, so a test never has to wait for the page itself.
// Note: The assembly is not strong named, and the package targets net10.0 only.
public class SeleniumTests
{
    // Two files are written: the page html and a png screenshot.
    // The converter waits for document.readyState itself before capturing, so nothing here has
    // to poll for the page to finish loading.
    // Not run by default: needs Chrome and a matching chromedriver, and the site under test listening
    // on http://localhost:5000
    [Fact(Skip = "needs Chrome and a matching chromedriver, and the site under test listening on http://localhost:5000")]
    public async Task Driver()
    {
        // Waits for the site under test to start before driving the browser.
        await SocketWaiter.Wait(port: 5000);

        var options = new ChromeOptions();
        options.AddArgument("--headless=new");
        options.AddArgument("--disable-lcd-text");
        using var driver = new ChromeDriver(options);
        driver.Navigate().GoToUrl("http://localhost:5000");

        await Verify(driver);
    }
}

==== interactions

Warning external-tool: Selenium needs Chrome and chromedriver: Selenium drives an installed Chrome through chromedriver, whose version has to match the browser, and the samples also need the site under test running.
